metadata.title: TIMSS 2023 Longitudinal User Guide for the International Database
metadata.venue: TIMSS & PIRLS International Study Center, Boston College / IEA

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The guide describes analyses using the TIMSS 2023 Longitudinal International Database with the IEA IDB Analyzer, which “seamlessly accounts for the sampling information” and uses the dataset’s multiple imputed achievement scores to compute accurate standard errors. For student-level analyses, the IDB Analyzer selects the appropriate sampling weight automatically, typically TOTWGT (and also SENWGT/HOUWGT as alternatives) and uses jackknife repeated replication design variables (JKZONE/JKREP) to estimate standard errors. For home and school context analyses conducted at the student level, the guide notes that student-level weights (e.g., TOTWGT) should be used after merging context files with student achievement/context files so that the required weights and achievement variables are present. For teacher analyses, the guide instructs users to merge teacher context data with student-teacher linkage files and to use teacher-specific weights (e.g., MATWGT_23/SCIWGT_23 or the 2024 equivalents) that are located in the linkage files, because teacher context files themselves do not contain sampling/weight variables.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The user guide is a documentation and example-analysis manual rather than an empirical ML study, and it does not provide a single explicit missing-data handling rule for the achievement PV estimation step (e.g., whether missing context items are imputed or excluded) in a way that can be mapped to a specific missing-data method category. Instead, it emphasizes that the IDB Analyzer uses the TIMSS longitudinal scaling outputs and “appropriate use of plausible values” and combines sampling variance with imputation variance. Therefore, the missing-data handling for the PV-based achievement estimation is not reported at the level of detail required by the schema.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The guide’s example analyses are produced using merged TIMSS 2023 Longitudinal Grades 4–5 data files (e.g., ASGALLM8L) and instruct users to select plausible values (Use PVs) and to check “Exclude Missing From Analysis” so that cases with missing values on grouping variables are excluded. For context scale analyses, it similarly instructs users to exclude missing values on grouping variables and notes that results may be suppressed when missingness is high (e.g., a reliability concern when data are available for less than 40% of students). For teacher analyses, it instructs users to analyze teacher variables only as student attributes by merging teacher context data with student-teacher linkage files and selecting the appropriate year-specific teacher weights.

data.outcome_summary: This TIMSS 2023 Longitudinal User Guide documents how to use the IEA IDB Analyzer to merge and analyze TIMSS 2023 Longitudinal International Database files for Grades 4–5 (2023 and 2024 time points) and, by extension, Grades 8–9. It explains that achievement outcomes are represented using TIMSS longitudinal plausible values (five PVs per scale for 2023, 2024, and change), and that the IDB Analyzer uses the sampling design information and combines sampling variance with imputation variance to produce standard errors. The guide provides example analyses including weighted country-level average growth/achievement, subgroup comparisons (e.g., girls vs boys), benchmark attainment percentages (Low/Intermediate/High/Advanced at fixed scale-score cut points), and context scale distributions using home and school questionnaire data. It also clarifies that teacher questionnaire data are not representative of teachers themselves; instead, teacher variables are analyzed as attributes of students taught by teachers with specific characteristics. The guide is methodological documentation: it does not present a predictive ML model evaluation, and therefore no ML performance metrics or causal claims are made.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is a user guide/technical documentation for the TIMSS 2023 Longitudinal International Database and the IEA IDB Analyzer, not an empirical ML research article. As a result, it does not define an ML target variable for prediction/classification, does not train or compare ML algorithms, and does not report ML performance metrics. The schema fields for ML techniques and main findings are therefore intentionally empty, while the weighting/PV/scaling procedures are described to support users’ secondary analyses.
